issues.description: The problem statement instructs students to initialize the SealSaloon attributes (e.g., the stock) in the constructor (problem_statement.md lines ~70-71), but later requires the stock attribute to be static (problem_statement.md lines ~77-80). Initializing a static field in an instance constructor is misleading/illegal as a recommended approach for beginners (static fields are normally initialized at declaration or in a static initializer). The solution implements the stock as a static final field initialized at declaration (SealSaloon.java: static final Stock stock = new Stock()), which contradicts the earlier instruction to initialize it in the instance constructor. This conflict can confuse students about whether stock should be instance-level or class-level and how/where to initialize it, potentially blocking correct implementation.
issues.suggested_fix: Clarify and make the requirement consistent: either (A) require a static (shared) stock and state that it should be initialized at declaration or in a static initializer (and keep acceptSupplyDelivery / calculateTotalPrice static), or (B) require an instance (non-static) final stock and instruct students to initialize it in the constructor. Update the problem statement to remove the contradictory sentence about initializing the stock in the constructor when the stock is specified to be static.

issues.description: The template and the solution use different getter names for StockIngredient, causing a name mismatch across artifacts. In the template, StockIngredient exposes getIngredientName() and Stock.findStockIngredient(...) calls getIngredientName() (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/StockIngredient.java and Stock.java). In the solution, StockIngredient exposes getName() and Stock.findStockIngredient(...) calls getName() (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/StockIngredient.java and Stock.java). This inconsistency between template and solution (method naming) can confuse students reading the solution or instructors comparing template and solution code, and may cause difficulty when porting or referencing code across artifacts.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the getter name consistent across template and solution. Choose one canonical getter name for the ingredient's name (preferably getName() to match common Java conventions) and update both the template and solution (and any usages such as Stock.findStockIngredient) accordingly. Alternatively, document the expected getter name in the problem statement so implementers know which to use.

issues.description: The StockIngredient 'name' field is exposed via differently named getters across artifacts: the template repository defines getIngredientName(), while the solution repository uses the conventional getName(). The problem statement asks students to "add getters for all the private fields" but does not prescribe the exact getter names, which makes the mismatch between template and solution an unintended naming inconsistency. This can confuse students about the expected getter name to call (e.g., when implementing or using Stock.findStockIngredient or when writing SealSaloon code) and forces them to reconcile two different identifiers for the same concept.
issues.suggested_fix: Use a single, consistent getter name for the StockIngredient 'name' field across template and solution. Prefer the conventional getName() (rename getIngredientName() -> getName() in the template and update any usages such as Stock.findStockIngredient to call getName()). Alternatively, if getIngredientName() is preferred, update the solution to use getIngredientName() everywhere. Document the expected getter name in the problem statement to avoid ambiguity.
